methods.canonicalBricks: Literal current canonical aliases only. No fuzzy musical equivalence.
methods.sections: Current form boundaries after the ABCA source audit; first A, second A, final A compared separately. Nine memberships are source-audited, 91 are harmonic-comparison inferences, so subgroup counts are conditional on current membership.
methods.aBrickFacets: A standard belongs to each canonical brick present anywhere in its first full A section. Duplicate same-name occurrences count once. Facets intentionally overlap.
methods.lastNonLauncher: Last first-A brick excluding any canonical name containing Launcher; fallback to literal final brick if none remain. This is a comparison only, not an assertion that Launcher is meaningless.
methods.centralA: Canonical brick overlapping the chronological midpoint of first A. If midpoint lies on boundary, choose newly starting brick.
methods.commonACore: First 75% of first A. Select present brick with highest document frequency across these A cores; tie by earliest onset.
methods.distinctiveACore: First 75% of first A. Select brick maximizing covered bars times log((101)/(1 + first-A core document frequency)); tie lexically.
methods.bBrickNames: Ordered canonical B brick names; adjacent same-name spans coalesced. Key and rhythm intentionally ignored.
methods.bBrickRhythm: Ordered canonical B brick names and normalized starts/durations; adjacent same-name spans coalesced.
methods.bChordSignatures: B roots relative to local entry key or first chord root. Exact includes register-aware intervals, explicit slash bass relative to anchor and source clipped flag; coarse uses major/minor/dominant/dim/sus quality. Starts/durations divided by B length where rhythm included. Values rounded to eight decimals; actual source durations in these excerpts are dyadic.
methods.bWindow: First overlapping chord in 2 or 4 equal B windows, relative to local entry key or first chord root. Coarse browsing signal only; not proof of full bridge equivalence.
methods.bOpeningKey: Use source key region covering the B-section start. Compute (entry-key pitch class - standard original tonic pitch class) modulo 12, retain entry-key Major/Minor. This is the local harmonic key area at B start, not necessarily the root/quality of the first B chord. References are to standard tonic, even when standard mode is Minor.
methods.bKeyRoute: Consecutive source key roots relative to standard tonic plus Major/Minor modes, coalescing identical adjacent key labels; ignore durations.
methods.bFirstLastKeys: First and final source key labels intersecting B, each root relative to standard tonic, preserving mode.

recommendation.primary: Offer overlapping A-brick facets sorted by count, and a separate B-entry-key grouping. These describe auditable source material without inventing a single central brick.
recommendation.secondary: A-ending is a useful alternate grouping only when explicitly labeled first A, second A, or final A. Endings differ in 84 of 100 standards across the three A sections.
recommendation.bridgeRefinement: Under B-entry-key groups, show key-route fingerprints and exact repeated B structures as refinements. Full B sequences are too fragmented to be the default hierarchy.
recommendation.avoid: Do not label same entry key or sampled coarse chord roots as equivalent full bridges. Do not drop Launcher bricks merely because they are common. Do not treat 91 inferred AABA memberships as independently source-verified forms.
